title: ATA does not imply AEA
text: Even dramatic cost compression in many goods and services, especially digital and cognition-intensive ones, need not translate into broad affordability of essential living conditions.

title: AI reorganizes scarcity
text: Under ATA, binding constraints tend to shift rather than vanish. The paper models this as a reallocation of rents across five layers: (1) physical resources, energy, and space, (2) infrastructure (power grids, compute, fabs, data centers, automation), (3) capabilities and high-trust organizational know-how, (4) rules and institutions governing access, and (5) jurisdictions supplying enforcement capacity and security. Layers 4 and 5 are analytically distinct: institutions are the rule systems governing access and control; jurisdictions are the territorial entities that give those rules coercive force and enforce them at scale.

title: Distribution follows ownership
text: Ownership and control cut across layers. The pattern of cross-layer claims held by firms, platforms, states, and households determines who captures the rents that persist under ATA, how gains split between capital and labor, and whether any meaningful degree of AEA emerges through wages, asset-linked claims, and transfers.
